digha.name: Digha
digha.description: West Bengal's most popular sea beach – a long stretch of hard sand at the Bay of Bengal

famousPlaces.name: Old Digha Beach
famousPlaces.description: The main beach with calm waves, perfect for swimming and sunset views

famousPlaces.name: New Digha Beach
famousPlaces.description: A cleaner, wider stretch of sand popular for long walks and water sports

famousPlaces.name: Marine Aquarium
famousPlaces.description: India's largest marine aquarium showcasing regional sea life

famousPlaces.name: Chandaneswar Temple
famousPlaces.description: Ancient Shiva temple 8 km from Digha, huge crowds during festivals

famousPlaces.name: Shankarpur Beach
famousPlaces.description: Quiet fishing village beach with casuarina groves, 14 km away

famousPlaces.name: Talsari Beach
famousPlaces.description: Where river meets the sea – serene backwaters and red crabs

famousFoods.name: Fresh Seafood Platter
famousFoods.description: Freshly caught pomfret, bhetki, prawns & crab – grilled or in light Bengali curry

famousFoods.name: Chingri Malaikari (Prawn Coconut Curry)
famousFoods.description: Prawns in rich coconut milk gravy – a coastal Bengali specialty

famousFoods.name: Ilish Bhapa (Steamed Hilsa)
famousFoods.description: Hilsa fish steamed with mustard paste – the prized monsoon delicacy of Bengal

famousFoods.name: Bhaja Muger Dal & Luchi
famousFoods.description: Classic Bengali breakfast of fried puffed bread with roasted moong dal

howToReach.summary: Most convenient – direct trains from Kolkata Howrah to Digha (3.5–4 hours)

steps.detail: Trains: Tamralipta Express (12858), Kandari Express (18001), Duronto Express. Platform check at enquiry counter. Trains daily.
Digha Flag Station is the terminus (~3.5 hrs). Auto-rickshaws outside for Old/New Digha (₹30–50).
Tamralipta: 6:40 AM from Howrah. Kandari: 2:25 PM. Book at irctc.co.in or Howrah booking counter.

howToReach.summary: Frequent AC & non-AC buses from Esplanade Kolkata to Digha (4–5 hours)

steps.detail: SBSTC, WBTC AC buses from Esplanade. Counter 1–4 for Digha route. First bus 5:30 AM, last 8:30 PM.
Greenline AC (₹350), SBSTC Volvo (₹320), Non-AC (₹180). Buses every 30–60 minutes.
Digha Bus Stand is central. Take auto (₹30) or walk 15 min to Old Digha Beach. Prepaid autos available.

howToReach.summary: Drive via NH16 – about 180 km, 4 hours from Kolkata

steps.detail: Take NH16 towards Kolaghat, then SH4 to Contai, then Digha–Contai Road. Total ~180 km, 4 hours.
Tolls at Kolaghat (~₹100). Parking at Old Digha Beach (₹50/day) and New Digha (₹30/day).

travelTips.title: Best Time for Sunset
travelTips.answer: Old Digha Beach offers the best sunset views. Reach by 5:00 PM in winter (4:45 PM in summer). The Marine Drive walkway is the prime viewing spot. Face west and look past the horizon for vivid orange skies.

travelTips.title: Swimming Safety
travelTips.answer: Swim only at Old Digha Beach where the slope is gentle. Avoid New Digha during high tide. Red flags mean no swimming. Lifeguards present at Old Digha 6 AM–6 PM only. Always swim within marked zones.

travelTips.title: Cash & ATMs
travelTips.answer: Carry cash – many beachside stalls don't accept cards. SBI ATM at Old Digha, HDFC ATM at New Digha. UPI (PhonePe, GPay) works at most restaurants. Withdraw in Kolkata before travelling.

travelTips.title: What to Carry
travelTips.answer: Sunscreen SPF50+, hat, sunglasses, light cotton clothes, flip-flops, light jacket in winter, and a rain poncho in shoulder season. Keep valuables locked in hotel; don't carry to the beach.

mandarmani.name: Mandarmani
mandarmani.description: India's longest motorable beach (13 km) – famous for red crabs, beach buggies, and serene sunrises

famousPlaces.name: Mandarmani Beach
famousPlaces.description: 13 km motorable beach – drive your car right on the sand

famousPlaces.name: Red Crab Beach
famousPlaces.description: Thousands of red crabs at sunrise – a photographer's delight

famousPlaces.name: Mandarmani Mohana
famousPlaces.description: Where the river meets the sea – serene backwaters and boat rides

famousPlaces.name: Shankarpur Fishing Harbour
famousPlaces.description: Colorful boats and fresh catch auctions at the working harbor

famousFoods.name: Fresh Crab Curry
famousFoods.description: Mandarmani's signature – fresh mud crab in spicy Bengali gravy

famousFoods.name: Fried Pomfret (Rupchanda Bhaja)
famousFoods.description: Whole pomfret shallow-fried in mustard oil with lemon – beachside classic

famousFoods.name: Tiger Prawn Malai Curry
famousFoods.description: Large tiger prawns in creamy coconut milk – a coastal delicacy

famousFoods.name: Bhapa Ilish (Steamed Hilsa)
famousFoods.description: Hilsa steamed with mustard paste and green chilies – Bengal's greatest seafood

howToReach.summary: Nearest station is Contai (Kanthi) – then 14 km by road to Mandarmani

steps.detail: Trains: Tamralipta Express (12858), Kandari Express (18001). Get off at Contai (Kanthi) Station, ~3 hours from Howrah.
Auto-rickshaws and shared jeeps from Contai Station. 14 km, ~₹150–200 per auto, 30 minutes.
Tamralipta: 6:40 AM from Howrah. Kandari: 2:25 PM. Book at irctc.co.in. Alight at Contai, not Digha.

howToReach.summary: Direct buses from Kolkata Esplanade to Mandarmani via Contai (5 hours)

steps.detail: SBSTC buses to Contai, then local bus to Mandarmani. Counter 5–6 for Contai route. Some direct buses available.
SBSTC AC (₹320 to Contai), then local bus (₹30). Total ~5 hours. First bus 6 AM.
Mandarmani More on Contai-Digha Road. Take auto (₹50) to beach, 4 km. Shared autos available.

howToReach.summary: Drive via NH16 to Contai, then 14 km to Mandarmani (4.5 hours from Kolkata)

steps.detail: NH16 to Kolaghat, SH4 to Contai, then Contai–Mandarmani Road. Total ~170 km, 4.5 hours.
Beach parking at resorts (₹50–100/day). Drive on hard sand at low tide only – check tide timings.

travelTips.title: Beach Buggy Rides
travelTips.answer: Beach buggies and ATV rides near the main beach entry. ₹300–500 per ride. Best at sunrise/sunset when the sand is firm. Avoid during high tide when the beach narrows significantly.

travelTips.title: Red Crab Spotting
travelTips.answer: Walk the beach at sunrise (5:30–6:30 AM) to see thousands of red crabs. Don't chase them – they burrow into wet sand. Best near the Mohana river mouth. Bring binoculars and a camera with zoom.

travelTips.title: Tide Timing
travelTips.answer: Check tide timings before driving on beach. High tide submerges parts of the 13 km stretch. Local resorts post daily tide charts. Best beach driving: 2 hours after high tide. Avoid evenings in rainy season.

travelTips.title: Cash & Connectivity
travelTips.answer: Limited ATMs in Mandarmani – carry cash from Kolkata or Contai. BSNL and Jio work well; Airtel patchy. Most resorts accept UPI. Stock up at Contai before entering Mandarmani village.

sundarban.name: Sundarban
sundarban.description: UNESCO World Heritage – world's largest mangrove forest, home of the Royal Bengal Tiger

famousPlaces.name: Sundarbans National Park
famousPlaces.description: UNESCO World Heritage core tiger reserve – accessible only by permitted boat safaris

famousPlaces.name: Sajnekhali Watch Tower
famousPlaces.description: Prime wildlife viewing tower with mangrove interpretation center

famousPlaces.name: Dobanki Watch Tower
famousPlaces.description: Canopy walk through mangroves – excellent for bird watching

famousPlaces.name: Netidhopani Watch Tower
famousPlaces.description: Scenic tower with views of tiger habitat and ancient ruins

famousFoods.name: Sundarban Mud Crab Curry
famousFoods.description: Freshly caught mud crab from the mangroves in spicy local gravy

famousFoods.name: Bhapa Ilish (Steamed Hilsa)
famousFoods.description: Hilsa from the tidal rivers, steamed with mustard paste – Bengal classic

famousFoods.name: Sundarban Wild Honey Dessert
famousFoods.description: Desserts with wild honey collected from mangroves – unique to this region

famousFoods.name: Narkel Chingri (Coconut Prawn)
famousFoods.description: Prawns cooked with grated coconut and green chilies – coastal village recipe

howToReach.summary: Train to Canning from Sealdah, then boat to Sundarbans (most common route)

steps.detail: Local trains to Canning: 1.5 hours. Trains every 30 min from Sealdah. First train 4:30 AM. Canning is the railhead for Sundarbans.
From Canning Station, auto/toto to Godkhali (45 min, ₹50). Godkhali is the main boat jetty for Sundarbans.
Permitted boats Godkhali–Sajnekhali (3–4 hrs). Shared boats ₹500–1000, private ₹3000+. Book via tour operator or forest dept.

howToReach.summary: Bus to Sonakhali or Namkhana, then boat into the mangroves

steps.detail: SBSTC buses to Sonakhali (3 hrs, ₹80) or Namkhana (4 hrs, ₹100). First bus 6 AM from Esplanade, Kolkata.
From Sonakhali jetty, boats to Sajnekhali (2.5 hrs). From Namkhana, boats to Bhagabatpur. Book at jetty or via tour operator.

howToReach.summary: Drive to Godkhali (110 km from Kolkata), then boat into the forest

steps.detail: Take Basanti Highway via Baruipur to Godkhali. ~110 km, 3 hours. Park at Godkhali jetty (₹50/day).
Book at Godkhali Tourist Counter or pre-book with Help Tourism, Sundarban Tiger Camp. Day trips ₹1500–3000 per person.

travelTips.title: Forest Permit is Mandatory
travelTips.answer: Get permits from the Forest Department at Sajnekhali or via tour operators. Foreigners need passport copy + visa. Apply 2 weeks ahead in peak season. Cost: ₹40 (Indians), ₹150 (foreigners). No permit = no entry.

travelTips.title: Hire a Local Guide
travelTips.answer: Mandatory for all safaris. Guides know tiger movement patterns, bird calls, and safe trails. Cost is included in most tour packages. Never enter the forest without a certified guide – it is also illegal.

travelTips.title: Best Wildlife Viewing
travelTips.answer: Early morning (6–9 AM) and late afternoon (3–5 PM) boat safaris offer best sightings. Visit watch towers at Sajnekhali, Dobanki, Netidhopani. Stay silent – noise scares wildlife. Bring binoculars.

travelTips.title: Carry Mosquito Protection
travelTips.answer: Mangroves have heavy mosquito and insect activity. Carry DEET repellent, full-sleeve clothing, and anti-malarial medication. Avoid scented products. Best to visit in dry winter months (Nov–Feb).
